newsitem.title: CHINA: China group calls for island action from Japan.
newsitem.headline: China group calls for island action from Japan.

text.p: A group of 31 Chinese journalists has demanded that Japan tear down the lighthouse built by a rightist Japanese youth group on one of a cluster of disputed islands in the East China Sea.
The group said in a statement that the building of the lighthouse on one of the Diaoyu islands, known in Japanese as the Senkakus, meant Tokyo had designs on invading China.

"The Japanese are once again opening their greedy mouths, their eyes covetously set on swallowing up all of China," said the statement, which was filled with references to Japan's World War Two aggression.

"If we fail to see this, we are giving tacit approval to the resurrection of Japanese militarism," the statement said. It called for unspecified military action from Beijing if Japan failed to destroy the lighthouse.
Beijing and Tokyo both claim the Diaoyu islands, which are about 300 km (190 miles) west of Okinawa and 200 km (125 miles) east of Taiwan. Taiwan also claims the islands.
The long-standing dispute over the uninhabited islands' ownership flared in July after the Nihon Seinen-sha (Japan Youth Federation) built a make-shift lighthouse on one of them.
The move drew protests from China's state media and calls for military action from anti-Japanese activists in Beijing, including a rare petition to parliament.
